response.reason: The three generic structures all use LEAGUE_ENVIRONMENT_BASELINE as the comparator and profile the opponent on goals_for/goals_against axes (HIGH/MID tiers). The candidate differs on three structural axes simultaneously: (1) the comparison is OPPONENT_PROFILE_INTERACTION — the cohort is TEAM_B's own away-game subset vs their overall away baseline, not the league mean; (2) the opponent profile axis is possession_for rather than goals_for or goals_against, which is a distinct conditioning dimension not present in any of the three generics; (3) the mechanism requires the opponent to be a possession-contesting side specifically, not merely a high-scoring or high-conceding one. These three differences together mean the statistical question being asked — does TEAM_B's possession and final-third entry rate compress when the away opponent is itself a high-possession side, relative to TEAM_B's own away baseline — is not structurally equivalent to any of the retrieved generics. The dual-metric joint target under the same possession_for opponent profile condition adds further incremental structure. KEEP is warranted.
